[ABOUT THE PROJECT]{.article-label}

::: {.lead}
This project investigates how embedded software and digital logic can cooperate to suspend a magnetic object beneath an electromagnet.
:::

## Scope

The design uses the course STM32L432KC and UPduino v3.1 boards, a browser interface through the course ESP8266, and three analog measurement channels. It divides floating-point position estimation and control from autonomous current regulation and fault supervision.

The repository currently contains a digital implementation, engineering documentation, software and HDL tests, calibration tooling, and a bench plan. Physical component selection and hardware validation remain ahead.

## Acknowledgements

The implementation and website were prepared with Codex assistance. The [AI-use statement](ai.qmd) describes the role and limits of that assistance.

## About this website

The report is authored in Quarto `.qmd` files. Its organization follows the supplied E155 portfolio reference: documentation, separate MCU and FPGA designs, results, AI use, and acknowledgements. Original technical notes remain available as detailed guides.

The visual system uses system typography, copper and muted green accents, a locally generated vector illustration, and responsive layouts. Interaction follows the supplied apple-design skill: immediate press feedback, familiar navigation, restrained motion, and accommodations for reduced motion, transparency, and increased contrast.
